mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from a sharp weekly trough, commuting-linked trips should increase discretionary stops and lift RETAIL_REC over the next month. The signal is strongest when TRANSIT is flat or recovering at the same time, because more trip chaining makes retail visits more likely.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises week-on-week after falling below its prior 2-week average
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped to -39.9 at t-1w then recovered to -25.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite a sustained WORKPLACES rebound and non-falling TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RESIDENTIAL indicates more time spent at home, which suppresses shopping and leisure outings and pushes RETAIL_REC lower within one to two weeks. When this home-stay signal strengthens, retail mobility should weaken even if other categories are stable.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above baseline throughout the snapshot and was 6.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated relative to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS jumps above roughly +15% from baseline, leisure demand is being reallocated outdoors, pulling activity away from retail and recreation venues over the following four weeks. This should appear as a negative retail response after a sustained parks surge.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 20.7 at t-0w after 14.6 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days after PARKS remains above +15 for at least one week.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES marks a tightening-mobility regime that reduces nonessential trips and depresses retail visits within one week. The effect is strongest when both series are below their prior two-week means, because the restriction shock is broad rather than sector-specific.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall below their 2-week averages
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -32.6 at t-1w and WORKPLACES was -39.9 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within 7 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move below their 2-week averages.

mechanism_narrative: An improvement in GROCERY_PHARM toward baseline signals catch-up essential shopping that can spill into nearby retail trips and raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. This mechanism should operate only when WORKPLACES is not collapsing, because severe commuting weakness overwhelms the spillover.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -8.4 at t-1w to -2.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM moves closer to zero while WORKPLACES stays near or above its recent level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS during warm-weather weeks indicates seasonal outdoor substitution that draws discretionary time away from malls and high-street retail, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next month. The signal fails when parks activity is merely a one-week spike without persistence.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above its prior week's level for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS increased from 5.9 at t-3w to 20.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days after PARKS remains elevated for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT normalizes first and then WORKPLACES follows, retail mobility should improve with a short lag because commuting corridors reopen before leisure spending does. The mechanism is strongest when TRANSIT is rising from a low base and WORKPLACES is no longer falling.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises week-on-week after being below -25
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -32.6 at t-1w to -25.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after TRANSIT rises from below -25 and WORKPLACES stops worsening.
